original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-zariski-descent-effective}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $S = \bigcup U_i$ be an open covering.
Any descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves
for the family $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}$ is
effective. Moreover, the functor from the category of
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-modules to the category
of descent data with respect to $\mathcal{U}$ is fully faithful.
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $S=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ an open covering. Given a family of scheme maps $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$, a descent datum for quasi-coherent sheaves is a collection of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-modules $\mathcal F_i$ with isomorphisms $\phi_{ij}:\operatorname{pr}_0^*\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal F_j$ on $U_i\times_S U_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on every triple overlap. It is effective if the $\mathcal F_i$ are obtained, up to isomorphism of descent data, by pullback of a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module. Then every such descent datum is effective and the canonical functor
$$\operatorname{QCoh}(S)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Desc}_{\{U_i\to S\}}(\operatorname{QCoh}),\quad\mathcal F\longmapsto(\mathcal F|_{U_i},\mathrm{can})$$
is fully faithful (indeed an equivalence of categories).
hypotheses: $S=\bigcup_iU_i$ is a Zariski open covering and $(\mathcal F_i,\phi_{ij})$ is a quasi-coherent descent datum satisfying the overlap cocycle.
conclusions: The descent datum glues to a quasi-coherent sheaf on $S$ and the restriction functor from $\operatorname{QCoh}(S)$ is fully faithful.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-descent-datum-cosimplicial}
Let $R \to A$ be a ring map.
Given a descent datum $(N, \varphi)$ we can associate to it a
cosimplicial $(A/R)_\bullet$-module $N_\bullet$\footnote{We should really
write $(N, \varphi)_\bullet$.} by the
rules $N_n = N_{n, n}$ and given $\beta : [n] \to [m]$
setting we define
$$
N_\bullet(\beta) = (\varphi^m_{\beta(n)m}) \circ N_{\beta, n} :
N_{n, n} \longrightarrow N_{m, m}.
$$
This procedure is functorial in the descent datum.
statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. An $A$-module descent datum is an $A$-module $N$ together with an isomorphism of $A\otimes_R A$-modules $\varphi:N\otimes_R A\xrightarrow{\sim}A\otimes_R N$ such that the two induced ways of transporting $N$ across three $A$-factors agree (the usual cocycle identity on $A\otimes_R A\otimes_R A$). Set $B_n=A^{\otimes_R(n+1)}$ for $n\geq0$. For $0\leq i\leq n$, define the $B_n$-module $N_{n,i}=A^{\otimes_R i}\otimes_R N\otimes_R A^{\otimes_R(n-i)}$ with $N$ in tensor position $i$. The descent isomorphism supplies compatible $B_n$-linear identifications $\varphi^n_{ij}:N_{n,i}\to N_{n,j}$ for $i\leq j$, and for an order-preserving map $\beta:[n]\to[m]$ there is a canonical $B_n\to B_m$-semilinear map $N_{\beta,n}:N_{n,n}\to N_{m,\beta(n)}$ sending $1\otimes\cdots\otimes n$ to the corresponding tensor in position $\beta(n)$. Define $N_n=N_{n,n}$ and
$$N_\bullet(\beta)=\varphi^m_{\beta(n),m}\circ N_{\beta,n}:N_n\to N_m.$$
Then $(N_n,N_\bullet(\beta))$ is a cosimplicial module over the cosimplicial $R$-algebra $B_\bullet$, and the construction is functorial in $(N,\varphi)$.
hypotheses: $R\to A$ is a commutative-ring map and $(N,\varphi)$ a module descent datum satisfying the cocycle identity.
conclusions: The stated assignments define a functorial cosimplicial $(A/R)_\bullet$-module.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-canonical-descent-datum-cosimplicial}
Let $R \to A$ be a ring map.
Let $M$ be an $R$-module. The cosimplicial
$(A/R)_\bullet$-module associated to the canonical descent
datum is isomorphic to the cosimplicial module $(A/R)_\bullet \otimes_R M$.
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a ring map and $M$ an $R$-module. Equip $N=A\otimes_R M$ with its canonical $A$-module descent datum, given by the evident reordering isomorphism $\varphi:(A\otimes_R M)\otimes_R A\to A\otimes_R(A\otimes_R M)$. Let $(A/R)_n=A^{\otimes_R(n+1)}$. Then the cosimplicial $(A/R)_\bullet$-module associated with $(N,\varphi)$ is canonically isomorphic to the cosimplicial module with degree-$n$ term $A^{\otimes_R(n+1)}\otimes_R M$ and structure maps induced by the standard maps of the cosimplicial algebra $(A/R)_\bullet$ acting trivially on $M$.
hypotheses: $M$ is an $R$-module endowed, after tensoring with $A$, with its canonical descent datum.
conclusions: The associated cosimplicial module is canonically $(A/R)_\bullet\otimes_R M$.

\label{lemma-with-section-exact}
Suppose that $R \to A$ has a section.
Then for any $R$-module $M$ the extended cochain complex
(\ref{equation-extended-complex}) is exact.
statement:
For a ring homomorphism $R\to A$ and an $R$-module $M$, the augmented Amitsur cochain complex is
$$0\to M\xrightarrow{u} A\otimes_R M\xrightarrow{d^0}A\otimes_R A\otimes_R M\xrightarrow{d^1}A^{\otimes_R3}\otimes_R M\to\cdots,$$
where $u(m)=1\otimes m$ and $d^n=\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(-1)^j\delta_j$, with $\delta_j$ inserting $1_A$ into the $j$th position among the $A$-tensor factors. If $R\to A$ admits a ring-homomorphism retraction $s:A\to R$ satisfying $s\circ(R\to A)=\mathrm{id}_R$, then this augmented Amitsur complex is exact for every $R$-module $M$.
hypotheses: The ring map $R\to A$ admits an $R$-algebra section/retraction $A\to R$.
conclusions: The augmented Amitsur complex $0\to M\to A\otimes_RM\to A^{\otimes_R2}\otimes_RM\to\cdots$ is exact for every $M$.

\label{lemma-recognize-effective}
Let $R \to A$ be a faithfully flat ring map.
Let $(N, \varphi)$ be a descent datum.
Then $(N, \varphi)$ is effective if and only if the canonical
map
$$
A \otimes_R H^0(s(N_\bullet)) \longrightarrow N
$$
is an isomorphism.
statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. An $A$-module descent datum is an $A$-module $N$ together with an isomorphism of $A\otimes_R A$-modules $\varphi:N\otimes_R A\xrightarrow{\sim}A\otimes_R N$ such that the two induced ways of transporting $N$ across three $A$-factors agree (the usual cocycle identity on $A\otimes_R A\otimes_R A$). \label{lemma-descent-descends}
Let $R \to A$ be a faithfully flat ring map, and let $R \to R'$
be faithfully flat. Set $A' = R' \otimes_R A$. If all descent data
for $R' \to A'$ are effective, then so are all descent data for $R \to A$.
statement: Let $R\to A$ and $R\to R'$ be faithfully flat ring homomorphisms, and put $A'=A\otimes_RR'$. Assume that every module descent datum for the base-changed ring map $R'\to A'$ is effective. Then every module descent datum for $R\to A$ is effective.
hypotheses: $R\to A$ and $R\to R'$ are faithfully flat; all $R'\to A\otimes_RR'$ module descent data are effective.
conclusions: All module descent data for $R\to A$ are effective.

\label{lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective}
Any faithfully flat ring map is universally injective.
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism of commutative rings. For every $R$-module $T$ the canonical map $T\to T\otimes_RS$, $t\mapsto t\otimes1$, is injective. In other words, every faithfully flat ring map is universally injective as a morphism of $R$-modules.
hypotheses: $R\to S$ is faithfully flat.
conclusions: $R\to S$ is universally injective/pure.

statement:
For a commutative ring $R$, define the contravariant $R$-module functor $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$, with $R$-action $(r\cdot\lambda)(m)=\lambda(rm)$. Then $C$ is an exact contravariant functor: for each short exact sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ the sequence
$$0\to C(M'')\to C(M)\to C(M')\to0$$
is exact. Furthermore, it reflects monomorphisms and epimorphisms: an $R$-linear map $u:M\to N$ is injective if and only if $C(u):C(N)\to C(M)$ is surjective, and $u$ is surjective if and only if $C(u)$ is injective.
hypotheses: $R$ is a commutative ring and $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$.
conclusions: The contravariant character-dual functor is exact and detects injections/surjections by reversing them.

statement: A homomorphism $f:R\to S$ of commutative rings is universally injective (or pure as an $R$-module map) if, for every $R$-module $T$, the canonical map $T\to T\otimes_R S$ is injective. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. For each one of the following properties, $M$ has the property over $R$ if and only if $M\otimes_RS$ has it over $S$: (a) finitely generated; (b) finitely presented; (c) flat; (d) faithfully flat; (e) finite projective (finitely generated projective). The same pure ring map $f$ is used in each assertion.
hypotheses: $f:R\to S$ is universally injective/pure, and $M$ is an $R$-module.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-standard-fpqc-covering}
Let $S$ be an affine scheme.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{f_i : U_i \to S\}_{i = 1, \ldots, n}$
be a standard fpqc covering of $S$, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-standard-fpqc}.
Any descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves
for $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}$ is effective.
Moreover, the functor from the category of
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-modules to the category
of descent data with respect to $\mathcal{U}$ is fully faithful.
statement: Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ be affine, and let $\mathcal U=\{f_i:U_i\to S\}_{i=1}^n$ be a finite standard fpqc covering: each $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$ is affine, and the map $\coprod_{i=1}^nU_i\to S$ is faithfully flat (equivalently, $R\to\prod_{i=1}^nA_i$ is faithfully flat). Given a family of scheme maps $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$, a descent datum for quasi-coherent sheaves is a collection of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-modules $\mathcal F_i$ with isomorphisms $\phi_{ij}:\operatorname{pr}_0^*\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal F_j$ on $U_i\times_S U_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on every triple overlap. It is effective if the $\mathcal F_i$ are obtained, up to isomorphism of descent data, by pullback of a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module. Then every such datum is effective and the canonical functor $\operatorname{QCoh}(S)\to\operatorname{Desc}_{\mathcal U}(\operatorname{QCoh})$ is fully faithful; in fact it is an equivalence.
hypotheses: $S$ is affine and $\mathcal U$ is a finite standard fpqc family of affine schemes with faithfully flat disjoint union over $S$.
conclusions: Every quasi-coherent descent datum is effective, and restriction to the covering is fully faithful.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{\varphi_i : U_i \to S\}$ be an fpqc covering, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-fpqc-covering}.
Any descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves
for $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}$ is effective.
Moreover, the functor from the category of
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-modules to the category
of descent data with respect to $\mathcal{U}$ is fully faithful.
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $\mathcal U=\{f_i:U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ an fpqc covering in the sense that it admits, over every affine open subset of $S$, a finite standard fpqc refinement by affine opens of its members. Given a family of scheme maps $\{U_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$, a descent datum for quasi-coherent sheaves is a collection of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-modules $\mathcal F_i$ with isomorphisms $\phi_{ij}:\operatorname{pr}_0^*\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal F_j$ on $U_i\times_S U_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on every triple overlap. It is effective if the $\mathcal F_i$ are obtained, up to isomorphism of descent data, by pullback of a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module. Then every such datum is effective. More precisely, pullback is an equivalence
$$\operatorname{QCoh}(S)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Desc}_{\mathcal U}(\operatorname{QCoh}),\quad\mathcal F\mapsto(f_i^*\mathcal F,\mathrm{can}),$$
in particular a fully faithful functor.
hypotheses: $\mathcal U$ is an fpqc covering of a scheme $S$, and the descent data are quasi-coherent with the cocycle condition.
conclusions: Every datum glues uniquely up to unique isomorphism and the pullback functor is an equivalence.
